name: cerebellum and basal ganglia overview
title: Movement disorders with normal power: a cerebellar lesion lets movement start but makes it inaccurate, on the same side, with the subdivision deciding the signs; a basal ganglia imbalance either blocks starting (Parkinson disease, hypokinetic) or releases unwanted movement (chorea, hyperkinetic); each column gives the signs and the circuit that failed

root.title: Abnormal movement, power NORMAL: cerebellum or basal ganglia?
lines: both are SIDE LOOPS: cortex → loop → thalamus → cortex · both also project to the brainstem
no upper motor neurons of their own, so NOT an upper motor neuron disorder
cerebellum: corrects errors + learns skills · basal ganglia: release wanted, suppress unwanted movement

groups.title: CEREBELLUM: movement starts, but is INACCURATE
lines: signs on the SAME side as the lesion
the REPAIR SHOP: masks lesions elsewhere · its own lesions last

groups.title: BASAL GANGLIA: release vs suppress is off
lines: globus pallidus fires at rest → inhibits thalamus
dopamine: direct pathway UP, indirect DOWN

head: h
Vestibulocerebellum
flocculonodular lobe
circuit: out: vestibular nuclei → eye, limb, trunk muscles

head: h
Spinocerebellum
vermis + intermediate zone
circuit: in: vision, hearing, skin + muscle afferents
out: fastigial and interposed nuclei → spinal cord

head: h
Cerebrocerebellum
lateral hemispheres
sign: • INTENTION tremor: near the end or holding a position
circuit: in: copy of the cortical motor command
out: dentate nucleus → motor and premotor cortex
tremor: long-loop reflex via cortex over-responds

head: h
Parkinson disease
HYPOKINETIC
sign: • tremor at REST: pill-rolling, hand first, eases with movement
• spared: practised or cued acts (rides a bike)
circuit: → too much inhibition of the thalamus
→ too little drive to motor cortex

head: h
Chorea
HYPERKINETIC
circuit: • too much L-dopa: direct pathway over-driven
→ too little inhibition of the thalamus

panels.title: Cerebellar circuit + motor learning
items: same circuit in every zone · half the brain's neurons
mossy → parallel fibres → Purkinje: weak, wide (~200,000 per cell)
Purkinje cells INHIBIT deep nuclei: the ONLY output
climbing fibre = error signal: teacher · parallel fibre = student
adjusts vestibulo-ocular reflex gain (aging, new glasses)
cerebellar patient + prisms: NO adaptation, no after-effect

panels.title: Basal ganglia circuit
items: out: globus pallidus → thalamus → motor cortex
direct: striatum inhibits pallidus → DISINHIBITS thalamus → movement
indirect: extra pallidal synapse + subthalamic loop → inhibits
pars reticulata → superior colliculus: eye movements
